([[White Plains, New York]]) | college = [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] (2021–2022) | highlights = * [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Rookie Team (2022) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2021]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2021) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|the {{USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship|FIBA Americas U16 Championship]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship|2019 Brazil]]|[[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Adrian Darnell "AJ" Griffin Jr.''' (born August 25, 2003) is an American [[basketball]] player . He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]] of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC). Griffin is a potential top five pick in the [[2022 NBA draft]] . ==High school career== Griffin played basketball for [[Archbishop Stepinac High School]] in [[White Plains, New York]].{{cite web |last1=Marks |first1=Brendan |title=A.J. Griffin is primed to be another in a long line of Duke stars |url=https://theathletic.com/1740404/2020/04/13/a-j-griffin-is-primed-to-be-another-in-a-long-line-of-duke-stars/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=June 17, 2021 |date=April 13, 2020}} As a freshman, he played with his older brother, [[Alan Griffin (basketball)|Alan]], and helped his team win its first [[Catholic High School Athletic Association]] (CHSAA) Archdiocesan title since 1984.{{cite web |last1=Thomson |first1=Josh |title=Boys basketball: Griffin brothers lead Stepinac to Archdiocesan title |url=https://www.lohud.com/story/sports/high-school/lohud-varsity-insider/2018/02/24/boys-basketball-griffin-brothers-lead-stepinac-archdiocesan-title/357725002/ |website=[[The Journal News]] |access-date=June 17, 2021 |date=February 24, 2018}} In his sophomore season, he and [[R. J. Davis]] formed one of the top backcourts in the nation.{{cite web |last1=McLamb |first1=Michael |title=Archbishop Stepinac finds new life with dynamic duo |url=https://www.marsreel.com/archbishop-stepinac-finds-new-life-with-help-from-dynamic-duo/ |website=Mars Reel |access-date=June 18, 2021 |date=February 13, 2019}} Griffin averaged 20.9 points, 10.9 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 3.5 blocks per game.{{cite web |last1=Drumwright |first1=Steve |title=AJ Griffin Hopes Continued Improvement in His Game Results in U16 National Team Spot |url=https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2019/05/aj-griffin-feature.aspx |website=[[USA Basketball]] |publisher=Red Line Editorial |access-date=June 17, 2021 |date=May 24, 2019}} As a junior, he averaged 17.7 points, 8.8 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 2.3 blocks per game, missing most of the season with a knee injury, and led Stepinac to the CHSAA Archdiocesan title. Griffin was sidelined for his senior season by an ankle injury.{{cite web |last1=Thomson |first1=Josh |title=Boys basketball: Stepinac's Adrian Griffin Jr., a Duke commit, may not return for senior season |url=https://www.lohud.com/story/sports/high-school/varsity-insider/2021/02/09/boys-basketball-duke-commit-adrian-griffin-jr-may-not-play-2021/4450027001/ |website=[[The Journal News]] |access-date=June 17, 2021 |date=February 9, 2021}} He was named to the [[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]] and [[Jordan Brand Classic]] rosters.{{cite web |last1=Krest |first1=Shawn |title=Duke Signees Paolo Banchero, A.J. Griffin Named McDonald's All-Americans |url=https://www.si.com/college/duke/basketball/paolo-banchero-aj-griffin-duke-mcdonalds-all-americans |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=June 17, 2021 |date=February 26, 2021}} ===Recruiting=== Griffin was rated a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], and a four-star recruit by [[ESPN]].{{cite web |last1=Watson |first1=John |title=The curious case of AJ Griffin and ESPN's rankings |url=https://247sports.com/college/duke/Article/The-curious-case-of-AJ-Griffin-and-ESPNs-rankings-164502577/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=June 17, 2021 |date=April 21, 2021}} On November 4, 2019, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] over offers from [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] and [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]].{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=2021 Chosen 25 wing A.J. Griffin commits to Duke |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/acc/2019/11/04/2021-chosen-25-wing-aj-griffin-commits-to-duke/40543607/ |website=[[USA Today]] |access-date=June 17, 2021 Beard|access-date=April 25, 2022 |date=April 24, 2022}} Griffin is a potential top five pick in the 2022 NBA draft . {{Cite web |title=Adrian Griffin Jr. |url=https://nbadraftroom.com/p/adrian-griffin-jr/ |access-date=2022-04-27 |website=NBA Draft Room |language=en-US}} ==National team career== Griffin represented the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] in Brazil. He averaged 13.5 points, 4.3 rebounds and 3.3 steals per game, helping his team win the gold medal.{{cite web |title=Adrian Griffin (USA)'s profile – FIBA U16 Americas Championship 2019 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/u16americas/2019/player/Adrian-Griffin |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=June 18, 2021}} Griffin scored 18 points against [[Canada men's national under-17 basketball team|Canada]] in the final.{{cite web |last1=Giles |first1=Matt |title=Gifted 15-year-old treasures Duke basketball offer, plans to visit |url=https://balldurham.com/2019/06/29/duke-basketball-offer-plans-visit/ |website=Ball Durham |access-date=June 18, 2021 |date=June 29, 2019}} ==Personal life== Griffin is a [[Christianity|Christian]] and often takes to social media to speak about his faith.{{cite web |last1=Doering |first1=Joshua |title=Freshman AJ Griffin boldly living as follower of Christ while leading Duke to Final Four |url=https://sportsspectrum.com/sport/basketball/2022/03/29/aj-griffin-follower-christ-duke-final-four/ |website=Sports Spectrum |access-date=2 April 2022}} Griffin's father, [[Adrian Griffin|Adrian]], played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for ten seasons before becoming a coach in the league, and serves as an assistant coach for the [[Toronto Raptors]]. His mother, Audrey, ran [[track and field|track]] for [[Seton Hall Pirates|Seton Hall]]. Two of his siblings have played college basketball: his brother, [[Alan Griffin (basketball)|Alan]], at [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] and [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]], and his sister, Aubrey, at [[UConn Huskies women's basketball|UConn]].{{cite web |last1=Waters |first1=Mike |title=Meet the Griffins: How family helped shape Alan, Syracuse basketball's exciting newcomer |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2020/11/meet-the-griffins-how-family-helped-shape-alan-syracuse-basketballs-exciting-newcomer.html |website=[[The Post-Standard]] |access-date=December 16, 2020 |date=November 13, 2020}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://goduke.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/aj-griffin/17231 Duke Blue Devils bio] *[https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/g/griffin-aj.aspx USA Basketball bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Griffin, AJ}} [[Category:2003 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Archbishop Stepinac High School alumni]] [[Category:Basketball players at the 2022 NCAA Division I Men's Final Four]] [[Category:Basketball players from Dallas]] [[Category:Basketball players from New York (state)]] [[Category:Duke Blue Devils men's basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:People from White Plains, New York]] [[Category:Small forwards]]
